summary.short: Proclamation 11002 (January 14, 2026) imposes a 25 percent Section 232 tariff, effective January 15, 2026, on imports of defined advanced computing chips ('Covered Products'), exempting listed uses such as U.S. data centers, R&D and startups, and directs trade negotiations and reports to the President.
summary.long: Proclamation 11002 under section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962, signed January 14, 2026, finds that imports of semiconductors, semiconductor manufacturing equipment and derivative products threaten national security. It directs the Secretary of Commerce and the U.S. Trade Representative to pursue trade agreements and to report within 90 days. It imposes a 25 percent ad valorem duty, effective January 15, 2026, on imports of 'Covered Products' (advanced computing chips and certain derivatives meeting the Annex parameters), with no duty for listed uses including U.S. data centers, R&D, repairs, startups, and non-data-center consumer, civil industrial and public sector applications. Annex U.S. note 39 defines covered semiconductor articles by total processing performance and total DRAM bandwidth, and defines a 'U.S. data center' as a facility requiring more than 100 MW of new AI load; new HTSUS headings 9903.79.01 to 9903.79.09 implement the duty and exemptions. Agencies may modify the HTSUS and customs procedures, drawback is unavailable, and the Secretary must provide a data-center market update by July 1, 2026. Broader tariffs may be considered after negotiations conclude.

notes: Only relations, entities and notes were requested; other sections are not annotated. The tariff applies to goods entered or withdrawn from warehouse on or after 12:01 a.m. EST on January 15, 2026 (clause 3). The 'U.S. data center' definition (over 100 MW of new load) appears only in Annex note 39(d), not in operative clauses. Annex note 39(d) lists subdivisions (i), (iii), (ii) out of sequence, and Annex items 14 and 13 appear in reverse order; the text also has OCR spacing artifacts in heading numbers (e.g., 9903.01 .25). No firms are named.

obligations.summary: The Secretary and the Trade Representative, with any senior officials they deem appropriate, shall jointly pursue or continue negotiations of agreements under section 232(c)(3)(A)(i) on imported semiconductors, semiconductor manufacturing equipment and derivative products; the President may consider significant tariffs and a tariff offset program depending on the status of those negotiations.

obligations.summary: Imports of Covered Products (advanced computing chips and certain derivative products listed in the Annex) are subject to a 25 percent ad valorem duty, in addition to other applicable duties, except for the listed end uses (data centers, repairs, R&D, startups, non-data-center consumer and civil industrial uses, public sector uses, and other uses the Secretary determines qualify).

enforcement.note: No fine, penalty, criminal sanction, licence revocation, benefit clawback, suspension or blocking provision found in the operative text. Clause (3) imposes a 25 percent ad valorem duty, clause (6) denies drawback, and clause (7) authorizes CBP to take measures to administer the tariff; none of these states a sanction for non-compliance. The Annex's U.S. note 39 and headings 9903.79.01-9903.79.09 set duty rates only.
